summary: Windows reopens a changed name in the focused Kit input for the same local actor, board and item. The input retains its exact text and entry spelling/revision; the accepted title and revision come from PostgreSQL. Closing does not submit. Drafts and submitted failures have independent lifetimes.
evidence: cargo test --locked -p boardcraft-desktop --features native-smoke --test windows_smoke -- --test-threads=1: all five graphical cases passed, none ignored or filtered. The new case drove real controls in fresh processes with an isolated local directory and checked both ordered item IDs, titles and revisions on fresh rustday_test connections at checkpoints.

Untouched entry closed and reopened clean. After typing ' Amber ' and closing the focused input, a different actor and a different board with identical item IDs each showed clean labels. The original scope reopened with that exact focused input only for item 17, no failure actions and zero submissions. Escape and another cold reopen left IDs 42 and 17 at Review/1.

The coexistence journey rejected three spaces, then closed an unsubmitted ' Amber ' editor on the same item. A fresh process restored the failure actions and focused input together without submitting. Escape cleared only the draft. A further process showed the original failed request and dismissed it without a write; both rows remained Review/1.

After a separate save to Indigo/2, the restored empty input retained entry Review/1. Enter with Review made zero submissions and displayed Indigo. With entry Indigo/2 and a separate save to Silver/3, reopen showed the exact ' Coral ' input over accepted Silver/3. Enter made one submission; a fresh read and clean cold reopen showed Review/1 above Coral/4.

Coordinator comparison: the isolated React cell restored the exact draft from its session store and, in a fresh session, from persistent storage. Untouched, actor/board isolation, Escape, coexistence, empty-input equality and the padded older-revision commit matched the Windows outcomes. The disposable reference save accepted the raw name from revision 2 exactly once. Windows uses a scoped local file rather than browser storage. InlineEdit compares against entry spelling; store::finish_name_edit accepts a known entry revision but also checks the last observed title under lock, so a different title written after load still conflicts. Live independent-window synchronization, signed-in access and end-to-end browser/HTTP were outside the comparison.

cargo test --locked --workspace passed, including desktop_edit conflict/retry and failed commit, all three local recovery tests (including stale draft cleanup), and both mobile service cases. cargo fmt --all -- --check, workspace Clippy with native-smoke and warnings denied, and git diff --check passed.

Coordinator runner verified 12-windows-name-draft: 15 runner regressions, three local recovery tests, save_failure_and_retry_at_the_row_boundary and five serial windows_smoke cases passed. All four earlier Windows journeys remained enabled; Android was not rerun. The Windows check used Kit window events and normal window removal, with a new database connection for each ordered readback. The reference checked both same-session component remount and fresh-session fallback; Windows checked fresh-process remount, not in-place navigation. Simultaneously retained drafts on multiple rows and slow local-disk behavior were not exercised.
